description: Check the links in a suspicious text message (smishing) or e-mail before anyone taps them. Paste the whole message or a single URL: every link is extracted, followed through URL shorteners to its real destination, and judged on observable signals — domain age from RDAP, impersonation of Korean banks/couriers/telecoms/portals and global brands incl. AI services such as ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini (brand keyword, lookalike spelling, or the brand domain worn as a subdomain), ClickFix pages (a fake "verify you are human" check that has the visitor paste a command into Win+R/PowerShell), Android APK downloads, punycode, public phishing/malware feeds, and DechoNet's own impersonation tracking. Use this when a user asks whether a link or message is a scam. Verdicts: danger, suspicious, unreachable, official (lands on the brand's own domain), no_signals (no warning signs found; this is not a finding that the link is safe). Reads landing-page HTML; inconclusive links may also run page scripts in isolated Chromium under the shared daily cap. DechoNet does not click, enter values or submit forms. The message text is not stored; requires no API key; rate-limited. Returns per-link verdicts with reasons and a shareable report link.

text.description: The link(s) to check — a URL, or the message text with verification codes, passwords and personal details removed (any language). Only the links are used (up to 5); the text is not stored.

receipts.description: Signed observation receipts behind this result, one per lookup: when, from where and under which rules version DechoNet observed it. Each url shows the record and checks its Ed25519 signature.
